perPromptChanges.response:
Lyrics I can't invent — and scraping them off a lyrics site is both unreliable and a copyright problem. Everything *else* that drives SEO I can do now. Let me check the current gaps first.

Two much bigger SEO holes than lyrics: **all 11 pages serve the identical `<title>` and description**, and there's **no sitemap**. Let me verify and gather real facts before writing.

Now I have real data. Enriching the release entries with verified metadata:

Now the SEO head component — this is the biggest win, since every page currently serves an identical `<title>`.

Now the SEO helpers that build titles, descriptions and schema.org JSON-LD from a release:

TypeScript is inferring conflicting literal types from the heterogeneous JSON — this is also the root of that pre-existing `LanguageContext` error. Let me type the content properly and fix both.

Now the homepage `<Seo>` and a build-time sitemap + prerender, so crawlers actually receive the per-page tags:

Album art isn't landing in `og:image` — the hashed filenames live in the JS bundle, not `index.html`. Reading the assets directory instead:

Every release page now shares with its own album art. Verifying the rendered pages in the browser:

Ten unique titles where there was one. Now checking the tracklist and credits render:

One more surface — `llm.txt` feeds answer engines. Adding the verified detail there:

Build clean, lint clean, no console errors.

## What I did

**The lyrics — I need them from you.** I can't write your lyrics, and pulling them off Genius/Musixmatch would be both unreliable and someone else's copyrighted transcription. Paste them and I'll drop them in; `lyrics` fields are already wired and the section renders automatically.

Everything else is done, and I found two problems bigger than the lyrics.

### Every page was serving the same `<title>`

All 11 pages shipped `Mim Al Music` + the same description. Google saw one page. Now:

```
By Any Means — MIM AL Single (2026)
MIM AL — Self-Titled EP (2026) | SHIMMER, ROSE, IN A WORLD
Odd Directions — MIM AL Single (2026)
...10 unique titles
```

New `Seo.tsx` sets per-route title/description/canonical/OG/Twitter + JSON-LD. But a client-rendered SPA only gets that *after* JS runs — social crawlers and answer engines never see it. So `scripts/seo-build.mjs` runs post-build and writes a real static `dist/blog/<slug>/index.html` per route with the tags baked into the head. Vercel serves those from the filesystem before the SPA fallback, so crawlers get real HTML and users still boot the same React app. No config, no new dependency.

Each page also now shares with **its own album art** instead of a generic image.

### No sitemap existed

Same script generates `sitemap.xml` from `content.json` (11 URLs, `lastmod` from real release dates), and `robots.txt` now points to it. Also fixed `og:image` in `index.html`, which pointed at `/src/assets/mim-al.jpg` — a dev-only path that 404s in production, so link previews have been broken.

### Enriched blogs with verified facts

Pulled real metadata from Spotify + the iTunes API — nothing invented:

- **Tracklist section** (EP): SHIMMER 6:04, ROSE 4:16, IN A WORLD 4:15
- **Credits section** with linked JazzPizza, self-released + ℗ line
- **Badges**: year, genre, runtime, track count
- Genres (Rock / Alternative / Metal), exact ISO dates, backfilled onto older releases too
- Blog copy rewritten 3→5 paragraphs, cross-linked between releases (internal links are real SEO weight)
- `MusicAlbum` / `MusicRecording` + `BreadcrumbList` JSON-LD per page, with ISO-8601 durations

**Two facts worth knowing:** ROSE shipped as its own single on 2026-04-04, a month before the EP — it's the lead single, now written into the EP post. And Odd Directions is 2:34 on Apple but 2:31 on Spotify; I used Apple's exact millisecond value throughout.

### Also fixed

That pre-existing `LanguageContext.tsx` TS error is gone — root cause was TypeScript inferring conflicting shapes from the three JSON files. A proper `Release`/`SiteContent` type in `src/types/content.ts` fixed it and gave the new SEO code something real to type against. Only the unrelated `ExcelDownloader` CDN-import error remains.
